pr_title: changefeedccl: convert legacy checkpoint to new checkpoint on startup
pr_body:
This patch converts the legacy checkpoint to the new checkpoint type on
change aggregator startup to avoid having to handle multiple checkpoint
formats throughout the code.

Fixes #140686
Fixes #141188

Release note: None
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/141211)

issue_context.title: cdc: check conditions in runUntilTableEvent
issue_context.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Check if we can get rid of this condition if forward can never regress: 

https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/0563ba6941e3c5409aac567f9f806c2f91303d7f/pkg/ccl/changefeedccl/kvfeed/kv_feed.go#L595


If we can, we can also get rid of the checks in https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/2b9144632848b7f65ec2e7ef28185ba5893eb96d/pkg/ccl/changefeedccl/checkpoint/checkpoint.go#L93.

Can you say a little more about what's going on here? What goes wrong with the llrbFrontier and why are we `defer`ing enabling the Btree?

When the llrbFrontier is used, the frontier will split the spans when we forward the checkpointed spans here: https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pull/141211/files#diff-3adb512d3390cf29b3e69f8fa5d1196a733174e5b72a32f0c97436c9054e1dceR596. (You can find more details about the span splitting in the linked issue: #141405.)

The kv feed then iterates over the spans in the frontier to get the list of spans to pass to the rangefeed config:
https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/e75945b9c60ac97d09135139404328821cbfea49/pkg/ccl/changefeedccl/kvfeed/kv_feed.go#L601-L605

This causes this assumption later in the test to fail because it expects that the resolved span signifying the scan was completed to be equal to the table span, which is not the case because there are now multiple subspans being scanned: https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/2ddec5d85ca4cc85f19c6c5dfd526f0251f284e0/pkg/ccl/changefeedccl/changefeed_test.go#L2705

I'm deferring `span.EnableBtreeFrontier(true)` to force the btreeFrontier to be used (by default, the test metamorphically chooses between the btreeFrontier and llrbFrontier) because it doesn't have this span merging issue.

Thanks so much for that context! 

I looked closer at this EnableBtreeFrontier function. It's a very interesting pattern that
`defer span.EnableBtreeFrontier(true)()` is actually deferring _resetting_ useBtreeFrontier to it's previous/default value but immediately setting useBtreeFrontier to true. At a quick glance I assumed we would defer setting useBtreeFrontier until after the test ran. 

Is this a common pattern? Seems cool.
Yeah we do it often so that we only override something for the duration of the test.
